newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to launch repo operations in mid-September.
newsitem.headline: Russia to launch repo operations in mid-September.

text.p: Russia's central bank plans to start repo operations in the Treasury bill market in mid-September, a senior central bank official said on Monday.
The central bank had a meeting on repos with Russia's 17 primary dealers on Monday, Konstantin Korishchenko, head of the central bank's open market operations department, told Reuters.
"The operations will be conducted only with primary dealers and with maximum care. Our goal is to test the mechanism," he said.

Korishchenko declined to give details, but primary dealers said it would allow eligible banks to fund purchases of Treasury bills from the central bank in the government securities trading system operated by the central bank.
Currently, banks trading in this system must have funds on their system accounts in order to buy bills.

But with repo operations, eligible banks will be able to buy T-bills even if they do not have funds on their accounts. The central bank will set a limit for these overdrafts for each bank, ranging from 20 billion to 50 billion roubles.
Banks running up an overdraft in this way will be granted a two-day repo. They will have to repay the overdraft over two days by selling T-bills with a 30-90 day outstanding maturity.
Only GKO discount T-bills, and not OFZ interest-bearing bonds, will be eligible.

The central bank will set the rate at which these bills can be repurchased every day at about 1000 Moscow time, before trading starts. But the central bank intends to keep the rate stable, and on most days will not change, dealers said.
